name: Question tags
note: The tag reverses the main clause: positive statement → negative tag, and vice versa (You're coming, aren't you? / He didn't call, did he?). It repeats the auxiliary (or do/does/did), and uses a pronoun.

questions.q: Sarah: 'You mustn't eat with your mouth full.' Paul: ' ______ '
options: Oh I have to, have I?
questions.fs: Sarah: 'You mustn't eat with your mouth full.' Paul: 'Oh I mustn't, must I?'

questions.q: The children don't have to come in right now, ______ ?
questions.fs: The children don't have to come in right now, do they?

questions.q: I've seen her act in many films but never live ______ stage.
questions.fs: I've seen her act in many films but never live on stage.

questions.q: Paul: 'I spent thousands on that car.' Sarah: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Paul: 'I spent thousands on that car.' Sarah: 'Oh you did, did you?'

questions.q: You still want to meet with him, ______ ?
questions.fs: You still want to meet with him, don't you?

questions.q: Some of Shakespeare's historical plays are rather long and so there are editions where they are ______ to make them shorter.
questions.fs: Some of Shakespeare's historical plays are rather long and so there are editions where they are abridged to make them shorter.

questions.q: It won't hurt ______
questions.fs: It won't hurt will it?

questions.q: Laurie can come by tomorrow, ______ ?
questions.fs: Laurie can come by tomorrow, can't she?

questions.q: As soon as he had invested the money, he became uneasy and was beginning to sense ______ about his investment.
questions.fs: As soon as he had invested the money, he became uneasy and was beginning to sense qualms about his investment.

questions.q: I think you ought to go ______
questions.fs: I think you ought to go don't you?

questions.q: There aren't many guests here yet, ______ ?
questions.fs: There aren't many guests here yet, are there?

questions.q: This project has only just been started and is in its ______ stages at the moment.
questions.fs: This project has only just been started and is in its early stages at the moment.

questions.q: They're selling their house ______
questions.fs: They're selling their house aren't they?

questions.q: The checks haven't been sent, ______ ?
questions.fs: The checks haven't been sent, have they?

questions.q: From childhood she has been stage ______ and was delighted when she got her first major part in the play at the national theatre.
questions.fs: From childhood she has been stage struck and was delighted when she got her first major part in the play at the national theatre.

questions.q: What ______ doing?
I'll be 13 tomorrow, ______ ?
Many of the safety instructions on things you buy often seem unnecessary and often quite ______ to the average person.
questions.fs: Many of the safety instructions on things you buy often seem unnecessary and often quite superfluous to the average person.

questions.q: In that case he'll have to look for a new job, ______ ?
questions.fs: In that case he'll have to look for a new job, won't he?

questions.q: Kathy's never impolite, ______ ?
questions.fs: Kathy's never impolite, is she?

questions.q: The secret of a good interview is to get straight to the point and ask ______ questions.
questions.fs: The secret of a good interview is to get straight to the point and ask incisive questions.

questions.q: You like milk in your tea, ______ ?
questions.fs: You like milk in your tea, don't you?

questions.q: He'd done that before, ______ ?
He's always been fascinated by the theatre and has spent many years doing odd jobs as a stage ______
questions.fs: He's always been fascinated by the theatre and has spent many years doing odd jobs as a stage hand.

questions.q: She's always late ______
questions.fs: She's always late isn't she?

questions.q: She's been very kind, ______ ?
You don't have to pay for it all at once as you can buy it in ______ stages.
questions.fs: You don't have to pay for it all at once as you can buy it in easy stages.

questions.q: You'd rather I kept quiet about it, ______ ?
questions.fs: You'd rather I kept quiet about it, wouldn't you?

questions.q: He's meeting me at 10 am, ______ ?
questions.fs: He's meeting me at 10 am, isn't he?

questions.q: All the ______ a stage said Shakespeare, meaning life is like a play in the theatre.
questions.fs: All the world's a stage said Shakespeare, meaning life is like a play in the theatre.

questions.q: It happened yesterday ______
questions.fs: It happened yesterday didn't it?

questions.q: She's from Korea, ______ ?
questions.fs: She's from Korea, isn't she?

questions.q: Fortunately she took no notice of the reviews of her acting and was quite ______ to some of the more sarcastic comments.
questions.fs: Fortunately she took no notice of the reviews of her acting and was quite impervious to some of the more sarcastic comments.

questions.q: You wouldn't want me to do that, ______ ?
questions.fs: You wouldn't want me to do that, would you?

questions.q: We didn't receive many calls this month, ______ ?
questions.fs: We didn't receive many calls this month, did we?

questions.q: He found himself at the edge of the cliff in a ______ position because one wrong step and he would fall into the sea.
questions.fs: He found himself at the edge of the cliff in a precarious position because one wrong step and he would fall into the sea.

questions.q: You are just the sort of person who would say that, ______ ?
questions.fs: You are just the sort of person who would say that, aren't you?

questions.q: There's not much news in today's paper, ______ ?
Although her boss knew that she was not telling the truth, her explanations for being late were always so reasonable and totally ______ that he believed her.
questions.fs: Although her boss knew that she was not telling the truth, her explanations for being late were always so reasonable and totally plausible that he believed her.

questions.q: She's definitely not coming ______
questions.fs: She's definitely not coming is she?

questions.q: You haven't forgotten, ______ ?
questions.fs: You haven't forgotten, surely?

questions.q: The whole event seemed very unnatural and had clearly been stage ______ appeal to the voters before the election.
questions.fs: The whole event seemed very unnatural and had clearly been stage managed appeal to the voters before the election.

questions.q: He really didn't need to speak to me like that, ______ ?
questions.fs: He really didn't need to speak to me like that, did he?

questions.q: We're having a barbecue next week, ______ ?
questions.fs: We're having a barbecue next week, will you come?

questions.q: Everything about the village was what you'd call ______ because all the houses were well looked after and reminded you of a time long since gone.
questions.fs: Everything about the village was what you'd call quaint because all the houses were well looked after and reminded you of a time long since gone.

questions.q: Sarah: 'You're being very rude!' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'You're being very rude!' Paul: 'Oh I am, am I?'

questions.q: We can't ask her again, ______ ?
questions.fs: We can't ask her again, can we?

questions.q: She suddenly stopped speaking to him on the phone and the conversation came to an ______ end.
questions.fs: She suddenly stopped speaking to him on the phone and the conversation came to an abrupt end.

questions.q: Sarah: 'I've torn up your homework essay!' Paul: ' ______ '
options: That would be nice, wouldn't it?
questions.fs: Sarah: 'I've torn up your homework essay!' Paul: 'That's nice, isn't it?'

questions.q: We've now ______ the stage where it's time to make our minds up.
questions.fs: We've now reached the stage where it's time to make our minds up.

questions.q: No-one understood that word ______
questions.fs: No-one understood that word did they?

questions.q: Although all the athletes were full of life at the start of the marathon, towards the end of the race a few were showing signs of tiredness and were clearly ______
questions.fs: Although all the athletes were full of life at the start of the marathon, towards the end of the race a few were showing signs of tiredness and were clearly flagging.

questions.q: Come back in the morning, ______ ?
questions.fs: Come back in the morning, will you?

questions.q: As he didn't want anyone else to hear what he was saying he spoke to her in a stage ______
questions.fs: As he didn't want anyone else to hear what he was saying he spoke to her in a stage whisper.

questions.q: Where ______ standing?
It's quite normal when you make your first speech in public to suffer from stage ______
questions.fs: It's quite normal when you make your first speech in public to suffer from stage fright.

questions.q: Sarah: 'I want you to give me some more money.' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'I want you to give me some more money.' Paul: 'Oh you do, do you?'

questions.q: Sarah: 'I can't take any more.' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'I can't take any more.' Paul: 'Oh, you can't, can you?'

questions.q: You said you would ______
questions.fs: You said you would didn't you?

questions.q: You must go ______
questions.fs: You must go mustn't you?

questions.q: He has his lunch at the office, ______ ?
questions.fs: He has his lunch at the office, doesn't he?

questions.q: You shouldn't have done that, ______ ?
questions.fs: You shouldn't have done that, should you?

questions.q: He used to work in the city, ______ ?
questions.fs: He used to work in the city, didn't he?

questions.q: Sarah: 'I won't listen to you any more.' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'I won't listen to you any more.' Paul: 'So you won't, will you?'

questions.q: Sarah: 'That's not allowed you know.' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'That's not allowed you know.' Paul: 'Oh it isn't, is it?'

questions.q: Sarah: 'She hates the sight of him.' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'She hates the sight of him.' Paul: 'She does, does she?'

questions.q: It drives you mad ______
questions.fs: It drives you mad doesn't it?

questions.q: Sarah: 'I would prefer to go by air.' Paul: ' ______ '
questions.fs: Sarah: 'I would prefer to go by air.' Paul: 'Oh you would, would you?'
